subject: Post-call: cloud private offer token economics & next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@greenbloom.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: cloud private offer token economics & next steps

Samir — thanks again for a constructive call this morning. Quick recap and a short checklist so procurement has what they need to start a private-offer review with AWS/GCP/Azure.

Key numbers we captured on the call:
- Expected steady-state consumption: ~2M tokens/day (avg) => ~60M tokens/month.
- Burst windows: +40-60% for product events (plan for 90M/month peak).
- Current target budget range (monthly): $11k — $15k.
- Target unit economics (your ask): $/1M tokens in the low-to-mid $20s net to Redwood; you flagged target ~$20-$24/1M before fees.

Marketplace mapping asks we promised to follow up on:
1) Net unit price after marketplace fees (AWS/GCP/Azure) for private offer pricing tiers.
2) How reserved capacity or committed-usage affects unit price.
3) Doc/contract template aligned to your procurement checklist so we can fast-track onboarding.

Attachments I uploaded for your review: pricing_workbook.xlsx (token model, three pricing scenarios A/B/C).

Next steps (proposed):
- Olga -> send marketplace fee-adjusted unit price scenarios and a recommended private-offer tier (today).
- Ben -> map shortlist of reserved-capacity commitments that yield target $/1M (by EOD).
- Samir -> introduce procurement@greenbloom.com to this thread so we can share an initial private-offer MOU and kickoff a channel onboarding request.

If that matches your expectation, I'll send an updated workbook with net unit prices that factor in marketplace fees and a suggested DocuSign MOU draft.

Thanks,
Olga

Subject: Re: Post-call: cloud private offer token economics & next steps

Thanks, Olga — that matches my notes. A couple quick clarifications before procurement digs in:

- Confirmed monthly baseline: 60M tokens (we can sign up to 12 months).
- If we commit to a 12-month reserved purchase, our procurement target is $15k/month budget cap. Goal is to get to ~ $20/1M after any marketplace fees — if that's realistic given Redwood's margins after reserved commitment, include that scenario.

procurement@greenbloom.com — looping you in. They will need:
- A pricing spreadsheet that shows gross list price, marketplace fee (%), and net $/1M tokens for AWS/GCP/Azure private offers.
- A redlined MOU or template PO to start internal review.

Can you also show a 3-tier option set (Conservative / Expected / Aggressive) with the commitment (6mo / 12mo) and what the net unit price looks like? We prefer simplicity (one line item: tokens/month + optional burst buffer).

Appreciate the quick turnaround on this.

Best,
Samir

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-06-30T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: marketplace fee scenarios + preliminary PPU mapping for GB-2027-118

Internal notes / do not share externally yet — quick pass on how marketplace fees and reserved commitments map to net ppu ($/1M tokens). I ran three scenarios in the attached CSV.

Summary (net $/1M tokens after marketplace fees):
- No commitment (hosted list): gross $/1M = $32 -> AWS fee ~12% -> net to Redwood ~ $28.2
- 12-month committed private offer, mid-tier: gross $/1M = $26 -> AWS fee 12% -> net ~ $22.9
- 12-month committed private offer + reserved GPU pool (higher commit): gross $/1M = $21 -> AWS fee 12% -> net ~ $18.5

Observations and recommended customer-facing options:
1) To hit Samir's target ~ $20/1M net, we need a 12-mo commit and to absorb a small portion of fee via discounted gross price (example gross $21-$22/1M).
2) Azure and GCP fees vary slightly; model attached includes 10–14% fee bands.
3) Recommend packaging as three clean SKUs: Conservative (60M/mo, 6mo), Preferred (60M/mo, 12mo), Aggressive (90M/mo peak buffer, 12mo + reserved pool).

Next actions for the thread:
- Olga: share a customer-facing spreadsheet that shows gross vs net ppu by cloud provider (I'll attach the marketplace-fee-scenarios.csv to our internal workspace).
- Marissa: prep the private-offer template (redwood-priv-offer-template.pdf) with a short MOU clause for onboarding on AWS marketplace.

Ben

Subject: Re: Post-call: cloud private offer token economics & next steps

Samir / procurement team — thanks for the quick confirmation. Attached are the customer-facing materials we discussed: updated pricing_workbook.xlsx with net PPU scenarios for AWS/GCP/Azure, plus a short Redwood private-offer MOU template (redwood-priv-offer-template.pdf).

High-level proposal (pick one SKU):
A) Conservative: 60M tokens/mo, 6-month term — gross $28/1M -> net after marketplace fee (AWS 12%) = ~$24.6/1M
B) Preferred (recommended): 60M tokens/mo, 12-month term — gross $22/1M -> net after marketplace fee = ~$19.4/1M
C) Aggressive: 90M tokens/mo (peak buffer), 12-month + reserved pool — gross $20/1M -> net after marketplace fee = ~$17.6/1M

If procurement can accept the Preferred or Aggressive SKU we can build an AWS private offer that shows the gross pricing line item and then AWS will apply their marketplace fee on the backend; Redwood will commit to the gross price in the private-offer MOU.

Link to sign initial MOU (preliminary): https://www.docusign.com/sign/ABCDEF-priv-offer-mou
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/GB-2027-118

Proposed timeline:
- Today: procurement confirms preferred SKU and any PO-specific language.
- 48–72 hours: Redwood generates private-offer template and submits to AWS marketplace onboarding with a channel request.
- 7–10 business days: marketplace private-offer review & acceptance (typical, may vary).

If that works I'll prepare the DocuSign MOU and set a 30-min follow-up this week to answer legal/procurement questions.

Thanks — Olga
